title: The Leadership Skill of Anticipating Resistance
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This entry frames anticipating resistance as a core leadership skill rooted in understanding how different audiences might negatively interpret a decision, action, or message. It offers a practical technique: asking what the worst or most negative interpretation of an upcoming decision could be, then listing out those interpretations before acting. A compensation-change example walks through several possible negative readings, from cost-cutting motives to distrust of leadership. The piece argues this preparation reduces defensiveness and helps leaders address objections before they surface.
points: Resistance drains energy and trust and redirects effort from results toward managing reactions.
Most resistance can be anticipated and defused before it appears by predicting audience interpretation.
The core technique is asking what the worst-case negative interpretation of a decision or message would be.
A compensation-change example illustrates how to generate and then address a list of likely objections.
Anticipating resistance makes leaders less defensive and less likely to take criticism personally.
quotes: Most resistance or controversy can be predicted and offset before it appears.
The skill of anticipating resistance is largely one of audience interpretation.

Asking What is the worst or most negative interpretation the primary audience could make of this decision, action, or message narrows the list of reasons and gives leaders insight into where resistance is likely to show itself.
The strongest leaders aren’t surprised by resistance or controversy.
Smart leaders know resistance is always the biggest obstacle they face.
